=== Critical response ===
{{Anchor|Critics}}On [[Rotten Tomatoes]], ''Inception'' holds an approval rating of 87% based on 363 reviews, with an average rating of 8.40/10. The website's critical consensus reads: "Smart, innovative, and thrilling, ''Inception'' is that rare summer blockbuster that succeeds viscerally as well as intellectually."<ref name="tomatoes">{{cite web|url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/inception/|title=Inception (2010)|work=[[Rotten Tomatoes]]| publisher= [[Fandango Media]]|access-date=January 22, 2021|archive-date=December 15, 2017|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20171215212221/https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/inception/|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Metacritic]], another review aggregator, assigned the film a weighted average score of 74 out of 100, based on 42 critics, indicating "generally favorable" reviews.<ref name="metacritic">{{cite web |url=https://www.metacritic.com/movie/inception |title=Inception |publisher=[[CBS Interactive]] |work=[[Metacritic]] |access-date=July 27, 2010 |archive-date=July 31, 2017 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20170731135208/http://www.metacritic.com/movie/inception |url-status=live }}</ref> Audiences polled by [[CinemaScore]] gave the film an average grade of "B+" on an A+ to F scale.<ref>{{Cite news|first=Andrew|last=Stewart|title='Inception' tops weekend box office|url=https://variety.com/2010/biz/box-office/inception-tops-weekend-box-office-1118021880/|work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|date=July 18, 2010|access-date=August 18, 2010|archive-date=September 17, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200917170505/https://variety.com/article/VR1118021880.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

[[Peter Travers]] of ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' called ''Inception'' a "wildly ingenious chess game," and concluded "the result is a knockout."<ref>{{Cite news| last= Travers |first= Peter |title= ''Inception'' |magazine= Rolling Stone|date=July 12, 2010|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/movies/reviews/17388/180225|access-date=July 14, 2010|archive-date=July 15, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100715051320/http://www.rollingstone.com/movies/reviews/17388/180225|url-status=dead}}</ref> Justin Chang of ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'' praised the film as "a conceptual [[wikt: tour de force|tour de force]]" and wrote, "applying a vivid sense of procedural detail to a fiendishly intricate yarn set in the [[labyrinth]] of the [[unconscious mind]], the writer-director has devised a heist thriller for [[surrealist]]s, a [[Jung]]ian's ''[[Rififi]]'', that challenges viewers to sift through multiple layers of (un)reality."<ref name="variety-review">{{Cite news |last=Chang |first=Justin|title=''Inception''|work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=July 5, 2010 |url=https://www.variety.com/review/VE1117943114.html |access-date=July 5, 2010}}</ref> Jim Vejvoda of ''[[IGN]]'' rated the film as perfect, deeming it "a singular accomplishment from a filmmaker who has only gotten better with each film."<ref>{{Cite news |last=Vejvoda |first=Jim |title= Inception Review: Christopher Nolan follows up The Dark Knight with his best film yet |work= [[IGN]].com |date=July 5, 2010 |url= http://movies.ign.com/articles/110/1103912p1.html |access-date=July 5, 2010 |archive-date=July 9, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100709073510/http://movies.ign.com/articles/110/1103912p1.html |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Relevant (magazine)|''Relevant'']]'s David Roark called it Nolan's "greatest accomplishment", saying, "Visually, intellectually and emotionally, ''Inception'' is a masterpiece."<ref>{{Cite news |last=Roark |first=David |title=''Inception'' |work=[[Relevant Magazine]] |date=July 12, 2010 |url= http://www.relevantmagazine.com/culture/film/reviews/22278-inception |access-date=July 14, 2010 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100721011123/http://www.relevantmagazine.com/culture/film/reviews/22278-inception |archive-date=July 21, 2010 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In its August 2010 issue, ''[[Empire (film magazine)|Empire]]'' gave the film a full five stars and wrote, "it feels like [[Stanley Kubrick]] adapting the work of the great sci-fi author [[William Gibson]] [...] Nolan delivers another true original: welcome to an undiscovered country."<ref>{{Cite news |last=Pierce |first=Nev |title=''Inception'' |work=[[Empire (magazine)|Empire]] |date=June 7, 2010 |url=https://www.empireonline.com/reviews/reviewcomplete.asp?FID=136118 |access-date=July 7, 2010 |archive-date=April 20, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110420044940/http://www.empireonline.com/reviews/reviewcomplete.asp?FID=136118 |url-status=live }}</ref> ''[[Entertainment Weekly]]''{{'}}s Lisa Schwarzbaum gave the film a B+ grade and wrote, "It's a rolling explosion of images as hypnotizing and sharply angled as any in a drawing by [[M. C. Escher]] or a state-of-the-biz video game; the backwards splicing of Nolan's own ''Memento'' looks rudimentary by comparison."<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Schwarzbaum |first=Lisa |title=''Inception'' |magazine=Entertainment Weekly |date=July 12, 2010 |url=https://www.ew.com/ew/article/0,,20401172, 00.html |access-date=July 13, 2010 |archive-date=July 14, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100714161259/http://www.ew.com/ew/article/0,,20401172, 00.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> [[Roger Ebert]] of the ''[[Chicago Sun-Times]]'' awarded the film a full four stars and said that ''Inception'' "is all about process, about fighting our way through enveloping sheets of reality and dream, reality within dreams, dreams without reality. It's a breathtaking juggling act."<ref>{{Cite news|last=Ebert|first=Roger|url=https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/inception-2010|title=''Inception''|date=July 14, 2010|work=Chicago Sun-Times|access-date=July 15, 2010|url-status=live|author-link=Roger Ebert|archive-date=April 18, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130418102245/http://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/inception-2010}}</ref> [[Richard Roeper]], also of the ''Sun-Times'', gave ''Inception'' an "A+" score and called it "one of the best movies of the [21st] century."<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.richardroeper.com/reviews/inception.aspx |title=''Inception'' Review |last=Roeper |first=Richard |author-link=Richard Roeper |work=Chicago Sun-Times |access-date=July 21, 2010 |archive-date=July 18, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100718103707/http://www.richardroeper.com/reviews/inception.aspx |url-status=live }}</ref> [[BBC Radio 5 Live]]'s [[Mark Kermode]] named ''Inception'' as the best film of 2010, stating that "''Inception'' is proof that people are not stupid, that cinema is not trash, and that it is possible for blockbusters and art to be the same thing."<ref name="Kermode">{{cite video |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/blogs/markkermode/2010/12/my_top_five_films_of_the_year.html |access-date=February 9, 2011 |date=December 24, 2010 |first=Mark |last=Kermode |author-link=Mark Kermode |title=Kermode Uncut: My Top Five Films of the Year |publisher=BBC |time=5: 05 |archive-date=April 9, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190409014641/https://www.bbc.co.uk/blogs/markkermode/2010/12/my_top_five_films_of_the_year.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

[[Michael Phillips (critic)|Michael Phillips]] of the ''[[Chicago Tribune]]'' gave the film 3 out of 4 stars and wrote, "I found myself wishing ''Inception'' were weirder, further out [...] the film is Nolan's labyrinth all the way, and it's gratifying to experience a summer movie with large visual ambitions and with nothing more or less on its mind than (as [[Shakespeare]] said) a dream that hath no bottom."<ref>{{Cite news |last=Phillips |first=Michael |title=''Inception'' |work=Chicago Tribune |date=July 15, 2010 |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/entertainment/movies/sc-mov-0713-inception-20100715, 0,6233986.column |access-date=July 15, 2010 |archive-date=August 11, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100811161957/http://www.chicagotribune.com/entertainment/movies/sc-mov-0713-inception-20100715, 0,6233986.column |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Time (magazine)|''Time'']]'s [[Richard Corliss]] wrote that the film's "noble intent is to implant one man's vision in the mind of a vast audience [...] The idea of movie going as communal dreaming is a century old. With ''Inception'', viewers have a chance to see that notion get a state-of-the-art update."<ref>{{Cite news|last=Corliss|first=Richard|author-link=Richard Corliss|title=''Inception'': Whose Mind Is It, Anyway?|magazine=Time|date=July 14, 2010|url=http://www.time.com/time/arts/article/0%2C8599%2C2003808%2C00.html|access-date=July 15, 2010|archive-date=July 18, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100718231754/http://www.time.com/time/arts/article/0,8599,2003808,00.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> [[Kenneth Turan]] of the ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'' felt that Nolan was able to blend "the best of traditional and modern film making. If you're searching for smart and nervy popular entertainment, this is what it looks like."<ref>{{Cite news|last=Turan|first=Kenneth|author-link=Kenneth Turan|title=''Inception''|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]|date=July 16, 2010|url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment/news/la-et-inception-20100716, 0,5478728.story|access-date=July 16, 2010|archive-date=July 28, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100728123450/http://www.latimes.com/entertainment/news/la-et-inception-20100716, 0,5478728.story|url-status=live}}</ref> ''[[USA Today]]''{{'s}} Claudia Puig gave the film three-and-a-half out of four stars and felt that Nolan "regards his viewers as possibly smarter than they are—or at least as capable of rising to his inventive level. That's a tall order. But it's refreshing to find a director who makes us stretch, even occasionally struggle, to keep up."<ref>{{Cite news|last=Puig|first=Claudia|title=You definitely won't sleep through complex thriller ''Inception''|work=[[USA Today]]|date=July 15, 2010|url=https://www.usatoday.com/life/movies/reviews/2010-07-15-inception15_ST_N.htm|access-date=July 16, 2010|archive-date=July 17, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100717231619/http://www.usatoday.com/life/movies/reviews/2010-07-15-inception15_ST_N.htm|url-status=live}}</ref>

Not all reviewers gave the film positive reviews. ''[[New York (magazine)|New York]]'' magazine's [[David Edelstein]] said in his review that he had "no idea what so many people are raving about. It's as if someone went into their heads while they were sleeping and planted the idea that ''Inception'' is a visionary masterpiece and—hold on ... Whoa! I think I get it. The movie is a metaphor for the power of delusional hype—a metaphor for itself."<ref>{{Cite news|last=Edelstein|first=David|title=Dream a Little Dream|work=[[New York (magazine)|New York]]|date=July 11, 2010|url=https://nymag.com/movies/reviews/67155/|access-date=July 13, 2010|archive-date=July 14, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100714165640/http://nymag.com/movies/reviews/67155/|url-status=live}}</ref> ''[[The New York Observer]]''{{'}}s [[Rex Reed]] said the film's development was "pretty much what we've come to expect from summer movies in general and Christopher Nolan movies in particular ... [it] doesn't seem like much of an accomplishment to me."<ref>{{Cite news|last=Reed |first=Rex |title=Can Someone Please Explain ''Inception'' to Me? |work=[[The New York Observer]] |date=July 13, 2010 |url=http://www.observer.com/2010/culture/can-someone-please-explain-inception-me |access-date=July 14, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100715052057/http://www.observer.com/2010/culture/can-someone-please-explain-inception-me |archive-date=July 15, 2010}}</ref> [[A. O. Scott]] of ''[[The New York Times]]'' commented "there is a lot to see in ''Inception'', there is nothing that counts as genuine vision. Mr. Nolan's idea of the mind is too literal, too logical, and too rule-bound to allow the full measure of madness."<ref>{{Cite news |last=Scott |first=A. O. |author-link=A. O. Scott |title=This Time the Dream's on Me |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=July 15, 2010 |url=https://movies.nytimes.com/2010/07/16/movies/16inception.html |access-date=July 15, 2010 |archive-date=July 17, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100717195917/http://movies.nytimes.com/2010/07/16/movies/16inception.html |url-status=live }}</ref> ''[[The New Yorker]]''{{'}}s [[David Denby]] considered the film to be "not nearly as much fun as Nolan imagined it to be", concluding that "''Inception'' is a stunning-looking film that gets lost in fabulous intricacies, a movie devoted to its own workings and to little else."<ref name="Denby">{{cite news|last=Denby|first=David|author-link=David Denby (film critic)|title=Dream Factory|url=https://www.newyorker.com/arts/critics/cinema/2010/07/26/100726crci_cinema_denby|access-date=February 10, 2011|newspaper=[[The New Yorker]]|date=July 26, 2010|archive-date=February 22, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110222212521/http://www.newyorker.com/arts/critics/cinema/2010/07/26/100726crci_cinema_denby|url-status=live}}</ref>

While some critics have tended to view the film as perfectly straightforward, and even criticize its overarching themes as "the stuff of torpid platitudes", online discussion has been much more positive.<ref>{{Cite web |first=Nick |last=Schager |title=Inception |url=https://www.slantmagazine.com/film/review/inception/4898 |work=[[Slant (magazine)|Slant]] |date=July 14, 2010 |access-date=May 27, 2011 |archive-date=August 8, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110808134156/http://www.slantmagazine.com/film/review/inception/4898 |url-status=live }}</ref> Heated debate has centered on the ambiguity of the ending, with many critics like Devin Faraci making the case that the film is self-referential and tongue-in-cheek, both a film about film-making and a dream about dreams.<ref>{{Cite web|first=Devin|last=Faraci|title=Never Wake Up: The Meaning and Secret of Inception|url=https://www.chud.com/24477/never-wake-up-the-meaning-and-secret-of-inception/| website= Chud.com|date=July 19, 2010|access-date=May 27, 2011|archive-date=May 12, 2011|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20110512083955/http://www.chud.com/24477/NEVER-WAKE-UP-THE-MEANING-AND-SECRET-OF-INCEPTION/|url-status=live}}</ref> Yet other critics, such as [[Kristin Thompson]], see less value in the ambiguous ending of the film and more in its structure and novel method of storytelling, highlighting ''Inception'' as a new form of narrative that revels in "continuous exposition".<ref name= Bordwell2 />

Several critics and scholars have noted the film has many striking similarities to the 2006 [[anime]] film ''[[Paprika (2006 film)|Paprika]]'' by [[Satoshi Kon]] (and [[Yasutaka Tsutsui]]'s 1993 [[Paprika (novel)|novel of the same name]]), including plot similarities, similar scenes, and similar characters, arguing that ''Inception'' was influenced by ''Paprika''.<ref name="Drazen" /><ref name="Wardlow">{{cite web |last=Wardlow |first=Ciara |title=The Synergy of 'Inception' and 'Paprika' |url=https://filmschoolrejects.com/the-synergy-of-inception-and-paprika-ffefd0973f12/ |website=[[Film School Rejects]] |date=March 2, 2017 |access-date=November 27, 2018 |archive-date=November 29, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181129123846/https://filmschoolrejects.com/the-synergy-of-inception-and-paprika-ffefd0973f12/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="IGN">{{cite web |last=Rizzo-Smith |first=Julian |title=An Ode to Anime Auteur Satoshi Kon |url=https://in.ign.com/paprika/127083/feature/an-ode-to-anime-auteur-satoshi-kon |website=[[IGN]] |date=August 24, 2018 |access-date=November 27, 2018 |archive-date=November 29, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181129124525/https://in.ign.com/paprika/127083/feature/an-ode-to-anime-auteur-satoshi-kon |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Boone |first1=Steven |title='Inception': As eye-catching, and as profound, as an Usher concert |url=https://www.politico.com/states/new-york/albany/story/2010/07/inception-as-eye-catching-and-as-profound-as-an-usher-concert-067223 |access-date=January 24, 2019 |work=[[Politico]] |date=July 16, 2010 |archive-date=October 26, 2017 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20171026182739/https://www.politico.com/states/new-york/albany/story/2010/07/inception-as-eye-catching-and-as-profound-as-an-usher-concert-067223 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Emerson |first1=Jim |title=Inception: Has Christopher Nolan forgotten how to dream? |url=https://www.rogerebert.com/scanners/inception-has-christopher-nolan-forgotten-how-to-dream | website=[[RogerEbert.com]] |date=July 17, 2010 |access-date=January 24, 2019 |archive-date= September 20, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130920030258/https://www.rogerebert.com/scanners/inception-has-christopher-nolan-forgotten-how-to-dream |url-status=live }}</ref> Several sources have also noted plot similarities between the film and the 2002 [[Scrooge McDuck|Uncle Scrooge]] comic ''[[The Dream of a Lifetime]]'' by [[Don Rosa]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Brown|first=Damon|title=Was 'Inception' inspired by Donald Duck?|url= http://www.cnn.com/2010/TECH/web/08/10/inception.donald.duck/index.html|publisher=CNN|access-date=December 29, 2011|date=August 11, 2010|archive-date=February 5, 2012|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20120205131026/http://www.cnn.com/2010/TECH/web/08/10/inception.donald.duck/index.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Gornstein |first= Leslie |title=Did Inception Really Rip Off Scrooge McDuck? |url=http://www.eonline.com/news/ask_the_answer_bitch/did_inception_really_rip_off_scrooge/193794 |work=[[E!#E! Online|E! Online]] |access-date=December 29, 2011 |date=August 4, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20120206031007/http://www.eonline.com/news/ask_the_answer_bitch/did_inception_really_rip_off_scrooge/193794 |archive-date=February 6, 2012 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Sean |first=O'Neal |title=The "Inception ripped-off Scrooge McDuck" theory that will briefly amuse you |url=https://www.avclub.com/the-inception-ripped-off-scrooge-mcduck-theory-that-w-1798221139 |work=[[The A.V. Club]] |access-date=December 29, 2011 |date=August 4, 2010 |archive-date=January 9, 2012 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20120109122833/http://www.avclub.com/articles/the-inception-rippedoff-scrooge-mcduck-theory-that%2C43814/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The influence of [[Andrei Tarkovsky]]'s ''[[Solaris (1972 film)|Solaris]]'' on ''Inception'' was noted as well.<ref>{{cite web | url= https://screencomment.com/2010/07/the-other-view-bowen-sounds-off-on-inception/ | website= screencomment.com | title= Inception – The Other View | first= Kevin | last= Bowen | date= January 16, 2020 | access-date=  | archive-date= December 10, 2020 | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20201210211304/https://screencomment.com/2010/07/the-other-view-bowen-sounds-off-on-inception/ | url-status= live }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal| first= Thorsten |last= Bothz-Bornstein |title= The Movie as a Thinking Machine| journal= Inception and Philosophy: Ideas to die for| year= 2011 |isbn= 978-0-8126-9733-9| page= [https://books.google.com/books?id=q62dW7vEjE0C&pg=PA205 205]}}</ref>

=== Year-end and all-time lists ===
''Inception'' appeared on over 273 critics' lists of the top ten films of 2010, being picked as number-one on at least 55 of those lists.<ref name="criticstop10">{{Cite web |url=http://criticstop10.com/best-of-2010/ |title=Home Page – Best of 2010 |publisher=CriticsTop10 |access-date=May 4, 2011 |archive-date=January 20, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120120185542/http://criticstop10.com/best-of-2010/ |url-status=live }}</ref> It was the second-most-mentioned film in both the top ten lists and number-one rankings, only behind ''[[The Social Network]]'' along with ''[[Toy Story 3]]'', ''[[True Grit (2010 film)|True Grit]]'', ''[[The King's Speech]]'', and ''[[Black Swan (film)|Black Swan]]'' as the most critically acclaimed films of 2010.<ref name="criticstop10" /> Author [[Stephen King]] placed ''Inception'' at No. 3 in his list of top 10 best films of the year.<ref>{{Cite magazine|title=Stephen King: The best films of 2010|url=https://ew.com/article/2010/11/26/stephen-king-best-films-2010/|last=King|first=Stephen|date=May 2, 2020|magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]]|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200929183213/https://ew.com/article/2010/11/26/stephen-king-best-films-2010/|archive-date=September 29, 2020}}</ref> Film maker [[Denis Villeneuve]] cited it as among his favorite films of all time.<ref>{{cite news |title=Denis Villeneuve's Favorite Movies: 29 Films the Director Wants You to See |url=https://www.indiewire.com/gallery/denis-villeneuve-favorite-movies/ |access-date=17 March 2025|work=IndieWire |date=26 February 2023 }}</ref> In 2025, the film ranked number 55 on ''[[The New York Times]]''{{'}} list of "The 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century" and number 24 on the "Readers' Choice" edition of the list.<ref name="Times"/><ref>{{cite web |title=Readers Choose Their Top Movies of the 21st Century |url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2025/movies/readers-movies-21st-century.html |website=The New York Times |date=July 2, 2025 |access-date=2 July 2025}}</ref>

Critics and publications who ranked the film first for that year included [[Richard Roeper]] of the ''[[Chicago Sun-Times]]'', [[Kenneth Turan]] of the ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'' (tied with ''[[The Social Network]]'' and ''[[Toy Story 3]]''), Tasha Robinson of ''[[The A.V. Club]]'', ''[[Empire (film magazine)|Empire]]'' magazine, and Kirk Honeycutt of ''[[The Hollywood Reporter]]''.<ref name="metacritictopten">{{cite web |url=https://www.metacritic.com/feature/film-critic-top-ten-lists |title=2010 Film Critic Top Ten Lists |last=Dietz |first=Jason |website=[[Metacritic]] |date=December 9, 2010 |access-date=January 30, 2018 |archive-date=January 4, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180104204524/http://www.metacritic.com/feature/film-critic-top-ten-lists |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Accolades ==
{{Main|List of accolades received by Inception}}

The film won many awards in technical categories, such as [[Academy Awards]] for [[Academy Award for Best Cinematography|Best Cinematography]], [[Academy Award for Best Sound Editing|Best Sound Editing]], [[Academy Award for Best Sound|Best Sound Mixing]], and [[Academy Award for Best Visual Effects|Best Visual Effects]],<ref name=oscars>{{cite web |url=http://www.oscars.org/awards/academyawards/83/nominees.html |title=Nominees for the 83rd Academy Awards |publisher=[[Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences]] |access-date=January 28, 2011 |archive-date=September 4, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120904121804/http://www.oscars.org/awards/academyawards/83/nominees.html |url-status=live }}</ref> and the [[British Academy Film Awards]] for [[BAFTA Award for Best Production Design|Best Production Design]], [[BAFTA Award for Best Special Visual Effects|Best Special Visual Effects]] and [[BAFTA Award for Best Sound|Best Sound]].<ref name="BAFTA">{{cite web |url=http://www.bafta.org/awards/film/2011-film-awards%2C1572%2CBA.html |title=2011 BAFTA Awards Nominees |publisher=[[British Academy of Film and Television Arts]] |access-date=January 28, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110110061729/http://www.bafta.org/awards/film/2011-film-awards%2C1572%2CBA.html |archive-date=January 10, 2011 }}</ref> In most of its artistic nominations, such as Film, Director, and Screenplay at the Oscars, BAFTAs and [[Golden Globes]], the film was defeated by ''[[The Social Network]]'' or ''[[The King's Speech]]''.<ref name=oscars /><ref name=BAFTA /><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goldenglobes.org/nominations/year/2010 |title=68th Annual Golden Globe Awards Nominations |publisher=[[Hollywood Foreign Press Association]] |access-date=January 28, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120911090824/http://www.goldenglobes.org/nominations/year/2010/ |archive-date=September 11, 2012 }}</ref> However, the film did win the two highest honors for a science fiction or fantasy film: the 2011 [[Bradbury Award]] for best dramatic production<ref name= Nebulas>{{cite web |url=http://www.tor.com/blogs/2011/05/2011-nebula-award-winners |title=2011 Nebula Award winners |date=May 22, 2011 |publisher=[[Tor.com]] |access-date=October 16, 2011 |archive-date=October 27, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111027030429/http://www.tor.com/blogs/2011/05/2011-nebula-award-winners |url-status=live }}</ref> and the 2011 [[Hugo Award for Best Dramatic Presentation#Long Form|Hugo Award for Best Dramatic Presentation (Long Form)]].<ref name=Hugos>{{cite web |url=http://www.thehugoawards.org/2011/08/2011-hugo-award-winners/ |title=2011 Hugo Award winners |date=August 21, 2011 |publisher=[[Hugo Awards]] |access-date=October 16, 2011 |archive-date=April 1, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160401000112/http://www.thehugoawards.org/2011/08/2011-hugo-award-winners/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

== In popular culture ==
Numerous pop and hip hop songs reference the film, including [[Common (rapper)|Common]]'s "Blue Sky", [[N.E.R.D.]]'s "[[Hypnotize U]]", [[XV (rapper)|XV]]'s "The Kick", [[Black Eyed Peas]]' "[[Just Can't Get Enough (Black Eyed Peas song)|Just Can't Get Enough]]", [[Lil Wayne]]'s "[[6 Foot 7 Foot]]", [[Jennifer Lopez]]'s "[[On the Floor]]", and [[B.o.B]]'s "[[Strange Clouds (song)|Strange Clouds]]", while [[T.I.]] had ''Inception''-based artwork on two of his mix-tapes. An instrumental track by [[Joe Budden]] is titled "Inception".<ref>{{cite web |first=Aaron |last=Zorgel |title=Why do rappers love the movie Inception so much? |url=http://www.aux.tv/2012/03/why-do-rappers-love-the-movie-inception-so-much/ |work=AUX.TV |date=March 8, 2012 |access-date=December 23, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160611062544/http://www.aux.tv/2012/03/why-do-rappers-love-the-movie-inception-so-much/ | archive-date=June 11, 2016 | url-status=dead }}</ref> The animated series ''[[South Park]]'' parodies the film in the show's tenth episode of its [[South Park season 14|fourteenth season]], titled "[[Insheeption]]".<ref>{{cite magazine|last1=Hill|first1=Scott T.|title=South Park Satirizes Inception's Mind-Wipe|url=https://www.wired.com/2010/10/south-park-inception/|magazine=[[Wired (magazine)|Wired]]|access-date=November 15, 2017|date=October 21, 2010|archive-date=November 16, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171116090714/https://www.wired.com/2010/10/south-park-inception/|url-status=live}}</ref> The film was also an influence for [[Ariana Grande]]'s video for "[[No Tears Left to Cry]]".<ref>{{cite web |last1=Willman |first1=Chris |title=Song Review: Ariana Grande's 'No Tears Left to Cry' |url=https://variety.com/2018/music/news/ariana-grande-no-tears-left-to-cry-review-1202770171/ |website=Variety |access-date=July 6, 2018 |date=April 19, 2018 |archive-date=July 14, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180714170349/https://variety.com/2018/music/news/ariana-grande-no-tears-left-to-cry-review-1202770171/ |url-status=live }}</ref> "[[Lawnmower Dog]]", the second episode of the animated comedy show ''[[Rick and Morty]]'', parodied the film.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Goldberg |first1=Lesley |title=Adult Swim's 'Rick and Morty' Takes On 'Inception' |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/adult-swims-rick-morty-takes-661896 |website=The Hollywood Reporter |date=December 6, 2013 |access-date=January 19, 2020 |archive-date=May 13, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200513145350/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/adult-swims-rick-morty-takes-661896 |url-status=live }}</ref> In an episode of ''[[The Simpsons]]'', named "[[How I Wet Your Mother]]", the plot spoofs ''Inception'' with various scenes parodying moments from the film.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.indiewire.com/2012/03/when-the-simpsons-went-inception-48463/|title=When 'The Simpsons' Went 'Inception'|last=Willmore|first=Alison|date=March 27, 2020|website=[[Indiewire]]|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200327074123/https://www.indiewire.com/2012/03/when-the-simpsons-went-inception-48463/|archive-date=March 27, 2020}}</ref> The showrunners of the television series ''[[The Flash (2014 TV series)|The Flash]]'' said its season 4 finale was inspired by ''Inception''.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.cinemablend.com/television/2423571/the-flash-showrunner-explains-how-the-finale-is-inspired-by-inception|title=The Flash Showrunner Explains How The Finale Is Inspired By Inception|last=Venable|first=Nick|date=February 7, 2020|magazine=Cinemablend|access-date=April 2, 2020|archive-date=July 11, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180711081429/https://www.cinemablend.com/television/2423571/the-flash-showrunner-explains-how-the-finale-is-inspired-by-inception|url-status=live}}</ref> In February 2020, American singer-songwriter [[Taylor Swift]] released a lyric video for her single "[[The Man (Taylor Swift song)|The Man]]", which featured visuals bearing resemblance to the film. The song also mentions DiCaprio in its lyrics.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://popcrush.com/taylor-swift-the-man-lyric-video/|title=Taylor Swift's 'The Man' Lyric Video Features a Subtle Nod to Leonardo DiCaprio|last=Reda|first=Natasha|date=February 7, 2020|magazine=[[PopCrush]]|access-date=February 9, 2020|archive-date=February 8, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200208183705/https://popcrush.com/taylor-swift-the-man-lyric-video/|url-status=live}}</ref> Kpop boy group [[Ateez]], also released a song titled "Inception" in 2020, serving as their title track for their fifth EP, [[Zero: Fever Part.1]]. The song is heavily inspired by Nolan's film, with the concept, music video and lyrics containing references to core concepts of "dream in a dream" and distorted realities that are present in the film.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rowley |first=Glenn |date=2020-07-30 |title=Ateez Dance Through a Dream in Explosive 'Inception' Video: Watch |url=https://www.billboard.com/music/music-news/ateez-inception-video-9427022/ |access-date=2026-07-01 |website=Billboard |language=en-US}}</ref>

The film's title has been [[Colloquialism|colloquialized]] as the word ''inception''<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 5, 2011 |title=inception |url=https://neologisms.rice.edu/word/44552 |access-date=February 8, 2026 |website=Rice University Neologisms Database <!-- from https://neologisms.rice.edu/aboutus -->}}</ref> and the [[Portmanteau|splinter]]<ref>{{Cite thesis |last=Lepic |first=Ryan |title=Motivation in Morphology: Lexical Patterns in ASL and English |date=2015 |degree=Ph.D. |publisher=University of California, San Diego |isbn=978-1-339-09169-3 |pages=213–214 |id={{ProQuest|1732684214}} (order no. 3725206)}}</ref> suffix ''[[wiktionary:-ception|-ception]]''<ref>{{cite web |date=November 25, 2013 |orig-date=Source of citation: Internet, July 2010 |title=-ception |url=https://neologisms.rice.edu/word/40915 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170705153941/http://neologisms.rice.edu/index.php?a=term&d=1&t=17573 |archive-date=July 5, 2017 |website=Rice University Neologisms Database}}</ref>, which refer to layering, [[Nesting (computing)|nesting]], or [[recursion]], in reference to the movie's key element of a "dream within a dream".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sherlock |first=Ben |date=August 4, 2024 <!-- 6:20 AM EDT --> |title=What Is Inception? Christopher Nolan Movie Title Meaning Explained |url=https://screenrant.com/inception-movie-title-meaning-explained/ |access-date=February 8, 2026 |website=ScreenRant |publisher=Valnet |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Heiden |first=Matt |date=February 17, 2012 |title=A translating tool for the modern "convo" |url=http://www2.portnet.k12.ny.us/SchreiberTimes/2011-2012/2012-2-17.pdf#page=13 |access-date=February 8, 2026 |work=The Schreiber Times |department=Features |publisher=the student body of Paul D. Schreiber High School |page=14 |publication-place=Port Washington, NY}}</ref> The normal meaning of ''inception'' is 'beginning', and the title refers to causing the inception of an idea within someone's mind.<ref>{{Cite web |last=L. |first=Naomi |date=January 21, 2015 |title=Four Words That Don't Mean What You Think They Do |url=https://jaycwolfe.com/2015/01/21/four-words-that-dont-mean-what-you-think-they-do/ |access-date=February 8, 2026 |website=The Wolfe's (Writing) Den |language=en-US}}</ref>
